tag: desk.documents cached byte-range reads #655544
description:
- New Bridge API `desk.documents` (capability `documents`) for reading
  large or binary files without base64-ing the whole file through a
  transform: `desk.documents.open(path)` returns a server-side handle (the
  path resolves like `desk.fs.*`: relative to the current Desk's directory;
  content is not read), `desk.documents.read(handle, {offset, length})`
  returns `{data: <base64>, eof: <bool>}` for a raw byte range (binary-safe
  -- unlike `desk.fs.readFile`, which decodes UTF-8 and throws on binary;
  `length` is clamped to 8 MiB per call), and `desk.documents.close(handle)`.
  Reads are cached Desk-side under `.desk_temp/documents_cache/`, keyed by
  the file's path, mtime and size, so a repeated range doesn't re-hit disk
  and a changed file is re-read rather than served stale. Raw bytes only (no
  format awareness); editing and live change notifications are not part of
  v1. A `kind: "python"` widget reaches the same service via
  `desk.shell.current_context.get_documents_service()`.

tag: porting existing apps guide doc #968159
description:
- New doc `tempui-porting-existing-apps.md` (linked from the main
  tempui doc: "for more information on porting existing app code to
  Desk"): a repeatable six-step process for figuring out how to port an
  existing project -- inventory its current directory structure, group
  into non-redundant porting units, gather grounded facts (what the
  target code does with file:line, what Desk already provides) before
  reporting any gap, parallelize read-only research but write the
  proposals in one pass, match the destination format's conventions,
  cross-link -- plus a "what Desk gives you" inventory by need (UI,
  inter-widget communication, files and large data, computation and
  long-running work, introspection) so "what does Desk already provide
  for X" is answerable from the doc itself, and a short list of known
  gaps (batch ingestion jobs with progress, external service
  dependencies).

tag: promoted widget rebuild re-reads widget.json #645093
description:
- A promoted widget's `[STALE]` rebuild (single instance, or "reload
  all stale") now re-reads `desk_widgets/<name>/widget.json`'s
  `"capabilities"` and `"state_schema"` and applies them to the
  widget's stored definition, so editing them and rebuilding works
  like any other source edit (before, the stored copy was frozen at
  promotion and the widget reloaded cleanly, then failed at runtime
  with a Bridge `403 ... lacks capability`). A capability you *add*
  asks the user for confirmation first (declining keeps the old list
  and still applies removals and schema changes); every applied change
  also raises a notification. A missing or malformed `widget.json`
  leaves the stored values alone. Never hand-edit the `.desk` file for
  this.

tag: dedicated hmsvc doc tempui-hmsvc.md #812810
description:
- New doc `tempui-hmsvc.md`: the full reference for Desk-hosted
  microservices -- the `service.json` schema, the `service.py` ASGI
  contract (and that `uvicorn` must be importable), discovery timing,
  the management-only networking model (`desk.hmsvc.list()` gives the
  `url`, the widget then calls `fetch()` itself), mandatory CORS,
  in-memory logs, and a minimal worked example. Linked from
  `tempui-custom-widgets.md` and `tempui-porting-existing-apps.md`.
  The `Desk-hosted microservices (hmsvc) #285553` entry below remains
  as the announcement; this doc is the reference.

tag: check new-features doc for thin feature docs #888639
description:
- `desk-temporary-ui.md` gained a navigation rule: when another doc
  covers a feature only briefly and you're about to write real code
  against it, read that feature's tag section in `tempui-new-features.md`
  first -- even for a tag your project has already seen -- before
  reading Desk's source or another project's code; and if you still had
  to read outside the doc set, say so and offer a FEEDBACK file.

tag: hmsvc dir live watcher + new service alert #008485
description:
- `desk_hmsvc/` is now watched live: a service directory you add,
  edit or remove while Desk is running is noticed without a project
  reopen or a manual Rescan click (the Microservices widget's Rescan
  button still works). A service not seen before in the project raises
  a top-right notification, "New microservice available: <name> --
  <description>"; clicking it places or focuses the Microservices widget
  (it does not start the service). Nothing about authoring a service
  changed. See `tempui-hmsvc.md`.

tag: OpenWithWidget optional label field #041937
description:
- `OpenWithWidget` takes an optional fourth, tab-separated field, a
  `label`: `OpenWithWidget<TAB>widget_id<TAB>path<TAB>label`. When
  present, the notification reads exactly the label instead of `Open
  <path>`, so a widget that doesn't consume a file no longer shows its
  placeholder path to the user. Existing three-field files are
  unchanged. See `tempui-open-with-widget.md`.

tag: hmsvc service url published to desk.state #095433
description:
- Desk now mirrors each microservice's `{"status", "url"}` into the
  shared state store as the key `desk.hmsvc.<name>`, updated on every
  status change (including a restart's new port). A widget that only
  holds the `state` capability can therefore learn a service's URL with
  `desk.state.get("desk.hmsvc.<name>")` (its `value`) or by subscribing to
  `desk.state.changed`, without declaring the broader `hmsvc` capability
  (which also grants start/stop/restart/logs on every service). A
  stopped or crashed service keeps its key with `url` null; one removed
  from disk gets status `removed`. These keys are runtime-only (never
  saved to the `.desk` file). See `tempui-hmsvc.md`.

tag: visual debugging of widget geometry guidance #733899
description:
- `tempui-custom-widgets.md` has a new section, "Debugging a widget's own
  rendering/geometry visually": a named pattern (a build marker in the
  widget's UI, a toggleable overlay recording real hit-test/render
  outcomes, ground-truth markers drawn via the same projection function,
  and closing the loop yourself with `desk_screenshot_widget`) for
  spatial bugs where what the user sees disagrees with where the code
  thinks something is. Guidance only; no API changed.

tag: named widget logs + log query MCP tools #211800
description:
- New Bridge capability `log` (and doc `tempui-widget-logs.md`): a widget
  calls `desk.log.append(name, [{ s, t? }])` / `desk.log.line(name, s)` --
  fire-and-forget (returns `undefined`, never throws) -- to append
  time-stamped strings to a named, in-memory log, and an agent reads
  them back with two new read-only MCP tools on the `desk` server:
  `desk_list_widget_logs` and `desk_query_widget_log` (inclusive
  `start`/`end` as ISO-8601 or epoch ms, `limit`, `order`). A `kind:
  "python"` widget appends through
  `current_context.get_widget_log_store()`. See `tempui-widget-logs.md`.

tag: recording events + timecoded transcripts #920929
description:
- Claude (Desk)'s record button now publishes the desk events
  `recording` (`{ recording_id, started_at_ms }`) and `stopped_recording`
  (`{ recording_id, started_at_ms, stopped_at_ms }`), which widgets can
  subscribe to via `desk.events` to know when to log. The transcription
  it pastes now starts with a note giving the relative path of a
  timecoded transcript, `.desk_temp/timecoded-transcripts/<recording_id>.txt`
  (`[mm:ss.mmm]` offsets plus the absolute `started_at_ms`), then the
  separator line `--- transcription ---`, then the transcription itself.
  Use the absolute times with `desk_query_widget_log` to see what a
  widget logged while a sentence was spoken. See
  `tempui-widget-logs.md`, "Recording events and timecoded transcripts".

tag: desk_git_commit MCP tool for commit messages #570472
description:
- New MCP tool `desk_git_commit(message, files?)` on the `desk` server:
  creates a git commit with the message passed as a structured parameter
  (fed to git on stdin, never through a shell), so apostrophes, backticks,
  `$(...)`, double quotes and newlines need no escaping -- prefer it over a
  Bash `git commit -m "$(cat <<EOF ...)"` heredoc, which can fail on an odd
  number of apostrophes. `files` is an optional list of exact paths
  (relative to the project directory, must stay inside it) to `git add`
  first; with none, it commits what is already staged. There is deliberately
  no add-everything option, no amend, and no `--no-verify`. A failure
  (nothing staged, a hook failing, not a repository) comes back as git's
  own output.

tag: python widgets use qt_controls, not QComboBox #514695
description:
- A `kind: "python"` widget embedded in the canvas must not use a
  native `QComboBox` (or a raw `QTreeView`/`QTreeWidget`'s branch arrows,
  or `QToolButton.setArrowType`): they paint with the platform style and
  open popups from untransformed screen coordinates, so under canvas zoom
  they scale oddly and a dropdown's list lands detached from its control.
  Use `from desk.shell.qt_controls import PaintedComboBox` (supports
  `addItem(text, userData)`, `currentIndex`, `currentData`, `itemText`,
  `currentIndexChanged`) and `PaintedBranchTreeView`/`PaintedBranchTreeWidget`
  instead. See "Project widgets" in this directory's own top-level doc.

tag: desk_ask_desk_expert MCP asks a Desk expert agent #748083
description:
- New MCP tool `desk_ask_desk_expert(question)` on the `desk` server:
  places a new Claude (Desk) widget whose agent knows Desk's own source
  checkout and docs and is told to answer your question *about Desk and
  this running session* (it may write diagnostic `kind: "python"` widgets
  to find out). Fire-and-forget: it returns the new widget's instance_id
  at once and nothing is sent back to you -- the answer appears in that
  widget for the user to read. Ask only when Desk's own behavior is the
  problem, not your project's. See `tempui-ask-desk-expert.md`.

tag: agent-raised desk events via MCP tool #028808
description:
- New MCP tool `desk_raise_event(name, payload?)` on the `desk` server:
  publishes a named desk event, with an optional JSON payload, onto the
  same `desk.events` channel widgets use, so a widget subscribed to that
  name receives it immediately -- no file for the widget to poll. The
  payload may be omitted (a bare signal) or carry what a file would have
  held; over about 1 KB, prefer a file and announce it with the event
  (hard limit 64 KiB). Names starting with `desk.` and `recording`/
  `stopped_recording` are reserved. The result reports how many widget
  instances were subscribed at publish time. See `tempui-agent-events.md`.

tag: agent waits for a desk event via MCP tool #196353
description:
- New MCP tool `desk_wait_for_event(name, timeout_seconds?)` on the
  `desk` server: blocks until a desk event with that name arrives and
  returns `{ status: "event", name, payload, sender, timestamp }` (or
  `"timeout"`, or `"ended"` if Desk was switched). With no timeout it
  waits indefinitely, so it is for a *background sub-agent* only: a call
  from the main conversation is refused by a hook (a foreground
  sub-agent is not detectable and is not refused). It is the receiving
  half of `desk_raise_event`: a widget publishes the user's answer with
  `desk.events.publish`, and the waiting sub-agent gets it with no file to
  poll. Listening lasts only while a call is in flight, so an event
  published between two calls is missed. See `tempui-agent-events.md`.

tag: events: bare signal or payload, file past 1 KB #504112
description:
- `tempui-custom-widgets.md` has a new subsection, "A signal, or the
  data itself", under "Sending and receiving named messages": a desk
  event can carry no payload at all (a message meaning "I updated the
  file") or can carry in its payload what you would otherwise have
  written to a file, so no file is needed; past about 1 KB, use a file
  and let the event announce it. It also notes that events are not kept
  for widgets that subscribe later. Guidance only; no API changed.

tag: [RELOAD] titlebar button on web widgets #696254
description:
- Every placed `kind: "html"` widget now has a `[RELOAD]` titlebar
  button that re-navigates just that instance's page (no rebuild, no
  confirmation). It occupies the slot the `[STALE]` badge uses: when an
  instance is stale `[STALE]` shows instead (that one rebuilds and
  reloads). You still cannot click either yourself -- but when a user
  needs a page re-run for a reason unrelated to a code change (a
  `desk.hmsvc` service that was not up yet, a changed `desk.state`
  value), point them at `[RELOAD]` instead of hand-building retry
  machinery into the widget.

tag: handoff request MCP tools #070658
description:
- New MCP tools on the `desk` server for handing a task to another
  agent or project without editing it yourself: `desk_create_handoff_request`,
  `desk_list_handoff_requests`, `desk_claim_handoff_request` and
  `desk_complete_handoff_request`. Requests move new -> in-progress ->
  complete and are stored as one markdown file each, so there is no
  directory-and-`mv` convention to invent. See `tempui-handoff-requests.md`.

tag: feedback item MCP tools #156881
description:
- New MCP tools on the `desk` server for Desk feedback:
  `desk_create_feedback`, `desk_list_feedback` and `desk_get_feedback`.
  Filing no longer needs the `../FEEDBACK/` filename convention, and a
  keyword list shows whether something is already filed (and its triage
  state: open, parkinglot, implemented, external). See
  `tempui-feedback-items.md`.

tag: installed job version hash skips .venv #284781
description:
- An Installed Job's version hash no longer reads the job's own
  top-level `.venv/` directory. A job with a large self-managed venv used
  to take seconds to hash and time out `desk_install_job` /
  `desk_run_installed_job`. Dependency versions still count: keep them
  pinned in `requirements.txt` (or a lockfile) outside `.venv/`. **Every
  python-kind job that has a `.venv/` gets a new version hash once, so
  call `desk_install_job` again before its next run.** See
  `tempui-installed-jobs.md`, "Self-managed venvs".
